incident-bot: P1 ALERT — eu-central-1 ALB health-check flap detected; 5xx spike from ingress (starting 1801000245). Synthetic checks failing (~30% of probes). Paging oncall.
Ava (oncall): on it. seeing increased 502/connection reset in Grafana for eu-central-1, spike started ~1801000200. Anyone touching ingress recently? @deploy-bot any deploys in last 30m? :eyes:
deploy-bot: last successful deploy: service/checkout v2026.03.15-0812 to eu cluster at 1800999400 (no automated canary failures). No direct ingress config changes in last 2h.
Miguel (netops): I'll check ALB target groups and NLB health. pulling target group health now. run:
```
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:eu-central-1:123456789012:targetgroup/ingress-tg/abcdef --region eu-central-1
```

Miguel (netops): output (trimmed):
```
TargetHealthDescriptions:
 - Id: i-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h, State: healthy
 - Id: i-0h7g6f5e4d3c2b1a, State: unhealthy, Reason: "Target.ResponseCodeMismatch"
 - Id: i-0z9y8x7w6v5u4t3s, State: unhealthy, Reason: "ConnectionError"
```

Miguel (netops): two instances in az-b failing health checks, connection resets reported. Could be Envoy or host networking.

Ava (oncall): Jia, can you look at ingress/Envoy in eu cluster? Sam, prep to scale ingress-controller if needed.

Jia (eng-runtime): looking at envoy logs for ingress pods in eu-central-1:
```
kubectl -n ingress logs deploy/ingress-envoy -l app=envoy --since=15m
```

Jia (eng-runtime): snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T08:10:12Z] error upstream reset: connection reset by peer
[2026-03-15T08:10:13Z] error 502 response from upstream
[2026-03-15T08:10:20Z] upstream connect timeout
```

Jia (eng-runtime): multiple Envoy worker threads showing upstream resets to checkout-service and catalog-service. Recent kernel upgrade? checking nodes.

Sam (infra): checking node-level network/eni metrics and recent kernel logs on affected hosts:
```
ssh ec2-user@i-0h7g6f5e4d3c2b1a sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 | tail
# dmesg shows tcp: excessive retransmissions
```

Sam (infra): I'm initiating a rolling restart of the ingress envoy pods in the affected AZ only to avoid global impact. Command:
```
kubectl -n ingress rollout restart deployment/ingress-envoy --selector=az=eu-central-1b
```

Ava (oncall): doing live mitigation: 1) restart envoy pods in az-b 2) temporarily set ALB to ignore unhealthy in that AZ by failing targets out of rotation (reduce traffic) 3) increase Envoy upstream timeout to 10s as a stopgap. @Miguel, can you adjust ALB target group weight or mark targets draining?

Miguel (netops): marking two problematic instances as draining via api (deregister-targets). running:
```
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn <arn> --targets Id=i-0h7g6f5e4d3c2b1a Id=i-0z9y8x7w6v5u4t3s --region eu-central-1
```

Miguel (netops): Deregistration commenced. ALB will stop sending new connections to those instances. Should shift ~12% traffic away immediately.

Ruth (customer-success): getting customer reports from EU customers: two mid-market customers reported checkout failures. Logged CS tickets CS-2031 and CS-2032. I've messaged both with acknowledgement and ETA 30m while we mitigate. :handshake:

Ava (oncall): run synthetic curl tests against ALB post-deregistration:
```
curl -I https://eu.redwood-inference.com/checkout -H 'Host: checkout.redwood'
```

Jia (eng-runtime): after restart and deregistration, curl returns 200 for most requests, occasional 502s (~2/100). Logs show fewer upstream resets. Monitoring graphs show 5xx rate dropping from 18% -> 3% over 10m.

Miguel (netops): also toggled cross-zone load balancing setting on ALB (enabled) to even out load across healthy AZs. That helped reduce impact on clients in az-c/d.

Sam (infra): scaling ingress-controller replicas in eu cluster from 3 -> 5 to increase capacity behind ALB. `kubectl -n ingress scale deployment/ingress-envoy --replicas=5`.

Ava (oncall): summary so far: root cause likely transient networking issue in eu-central-1b hosts causing Envoy upstream connection resets; mitigation: deregister bad hosts, restart Envoy pods in az-b, enable cross-zone load balancing, scale replicas, raised Envoy timeouts. Customer-facing impact: about 12% traffic degraded for ~45m, targeted impact to checkout endpoints for 2 known customers (CS-2031/2032). Paging cleared at 1801001380. Leaving thread open for handoff to postmortem.

Jia (eng-runtime): collecting heap/proc metrics and core dumps from affected pods and saving to S3: s3://redwood-incidents/1801000245/ for postmortem.

Miguel (netops): I'll follow up with cloud provider on the EC2 network errors and file a case for the AZ. Ticket: AWS-CASE-88421

Ava (oncall): handing off to oncall-backfill @Sam for next 2h to monitor and prepare postmortem. Action items:
 - Sam: confirm host network health in az-b and re-register targets only when stable (ETA 2h)
 - Jia: investigate Envoy upstream timeouts and whether we need a config change (ETA 24h)
 - Miguel: follow up with AWS and update ticket (ETA 4h)
 - Ruth: outreach to affected customers with incident summary (ETA 1h)

Sam (infra): acknowledged, monitoring dashboards and will keep an eye on 5xx. :eyes:

Ruth (customer-success): sending a short customer note now; will include expected remediation and next steps. cc: execs.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: P1 -> Mitigated (partial) at 1801001380. Postmortem owner: Jia (eng-runtime). SLA impact: transient errors for some customers, investigating root cause; follow-up postmortem scheduled.

Ava (oncall): closing live paging. Thanks team. We'll draft a postmortem with timeline and remediation to avoid AZ-level single points. :thumbsup:
